questions.q: What is a Tableau dashboard, as distinct from a worksheet?
options: A static image export of a single worksheet
A combination of worksheets, filters, and objects assembled onto one canvas so a viewer can see and interact with several related answers at once
A separate workbook file that must be opened independently
A second copy of the same worksheet with different colors
questions.explain: A dashboard combines multiple worksheets (plus filters and objects) into one interactive canvas — the actual deliverable most BI Developer and Data Analyst jobs ask for.

questions.q: When you drag a worksheet onto a dashboard and later edit that worksheet's calculated field on its own tab, what happens to the dashboard?
options: The dashboard breaks and must be rebuilt from scratch
Nothing — the dashboard keeps a frozen snapshot from when it was dragged in
The dashboard zone updates immediately, since it's a live window onto the same worksheet, not a picture of it
You have to manually re-drag the worksheet back onto the dashboard
questions.explain: Dashboard zones stay live — any change to the underlying worksheet (formatting, filters, calculations) reflects immediately wherever that worksheet appears on a dashboard.

questions.q: Why does this lesson recommend a Range or Fixed size over Automatic sizing for your first professional dashboard?
options: Automatic sizing keeps resizing the canvas as you work, which makes precise layout tasks like containers and KPI headers much harder to get right
Range sizing disables all dashboard actions
Automatic sizing is only available in Tableau Public, not Desktop
Fixed sizing is required before any worksheet can be added at all
questions.explain: Automatic sizing stretches to fill whatever screen displays it, which sounds flexible but makes precise layout work unpredictable — Range or Fixed sizing gives you a stable canvas to build on.

questions.q: According to the 5-step build order in this lesson, what should you do BEFORE dragging any worksheet onto a new dashboard?
options: Finish every worksheet's formatting on its own tab, and set the dashboard's size
Delete all existing worksheets in the workbook
Add the KPI header and global filters
Publish the workbook to Tableau Server
questions.explain: The recommended order is: finish worksheets first, set the dashboard size before dragging anything in, place the most important view first, add supporting views, then add the KPI header and global filters last.

questions.q: In the real Tableau screenshot in this lesson, what interaction is being shown?
options: Connecting Tableau to a SQL Server database
Publishing a dashboard to Tableau Cloud
Editing a calculated field's formula
Dragging a worksheet from the Sheets list in the Dashboard pane onto the dashboard canvas
questions.explain: The screenshot, from Tableau's own help documentation, shows a worksheet named "Forecast" being dragged from the Sheets list onto the dashboard canvas — the core interaction behind building any dashboard.
